review_candidates.title: Director, Program Implementation - Northeast
review_candidates.description: Title: Director, Program Implementation - Northeast Location: Northeast region required (New York City or Rhode Island preferred); up to 40% travel throughout the broader Northeast region required. Job Band: Level 3 Reports to : Aisha Chappell, VP Program Implementation - Northeast Start Date: Early November Who We Are Blue Engine is an education non-profit focused on ending the long-standing pattern of disproportionate student outcomes by shifting the paradigm of “typical teaching.” Blue Engine partners with schools and systems to elevate educators' mindsets and skills, ensuring all students can access and engage in grade-level learning in every lesson. We support educators in effectively teaching to learner variability by supporting the development of 1) inclusive mindsets & practices, 2) effective co-teaching and educator collaboration, and 3) data-driven teacher development systems. Our product offerings support school and systems leaders in system and school-level planning and design, instructional leader development, and content-driven teacher development. The Role Blue Engine is seeking a Northeast-based Director of Implementation to implement Blue Engine’s products across the region, with much of the portfolio expected to be NYC-based. The Director of Implementation will lead the contextualization and implementation of our cohort products, supporting educators and leaders in using data effectively, delivering instruction that meets learner needs, and strengthening collaboration and co-planning. The coach will directly support partnership launch, job-embedded development, and data-to-action planning for our cohort products. Additionally, the Director of Implementation will lead professional learning and serve as a project team member, supporting systems to develop effective enabling conditions for inclusive instruction. This role is ideal for someone passionate about instructional coaching and creating inclusive classrooms for all learners. Primary Responsibilities & Outcomes: I. Partner Implementation and Impact | 75% 1. Lead direct implementation that changes educator and leader practice Internalize, contextualize, and deliver Blue Engine products with integrity across an assigned portfolio. Facilitate professional learning, communities of practice, coaching cycles, and strategic-planning sessions for teachers, instructional coaches, and school and district leaders. Coach educators on the technical practices, adaptive mindsets, and team dynamics for inclusive instruction. Support partners to strengthen the systems, routines, and enabling conditions that sustain changes in practice. Adapt implementation to partner context while protecting the core product elements required for impact. Work effectively across grade levels and content areas, drawing on internal or external expertise when specialized content knowledge is required. 2. Own implementation progress and impact across an assigned portfolio Develop and execute implementation plans aligned to partner goals and Blue Engine product objectives. Establish clear roles, expectations, decision-making, and measures of success with partner stakeholders. Coordinate schedules, communications, deliverables, data, and follow-up across concurrent partnerships. Monitor implementation progress and proactively identify risks, barriers, and emerging needs. Communicate directly when partner decisions, practices, or conditions put intended outcomes at risk. Diagnose root causes, adjust strategy, and escalate issues beyond the role’s authority or locus of control. Build authentic, accountable relationships that support engagement, learning, and implementation progress. 3. Use evidence to guide implementation and demonstrate impact Collect and analyze implementation, perception, practice, and student-outcome data. Use multiple data sources to identify progress, disparities, root causes, and opportunities for improvement. Adjust professional learning, coaching, and partnership strategy in response to evidence. Lead progress-monitoring conversations that help partners interpret evidence and determine next actions. Translate evidence into a clear and appropriately qualified story of implementation progress and impact. Maintain timely and accurate implementation records and portfolio updates. Provide Partnership Development leaders with evidence, partner context, risks, and recommendations that inform renewal and expansion decisions. II. Product and Organizational Contribution | 25% 1. Strengthen Blue Engine’s products and implementation model Pilot product updates in authentic partner contexts. Provide specific, evidence-based feedback on product usability, feasibility, contextual relevance, and impact. Identify patterns across partnerships that may warrant product improvement or additional guidance. 2. Contribute to cross-functional collaboration and shared learning Collaborate with Program, Product, and Partnership Development colleagues to solve implementation challenges and improve partner outcomes. Share lessons, effective practices, and implementation risks across partnerships. Participate actively in required team and organization-wide collaboration structures. Support the development of shared tools, routines, and standards that improve implementation quality. 3. Contribute to Blue Engine’s culture Give and receive candid, constructive feedback across roles and levels. Follow through on commitments and contribute to a culture of accountability, learning, and improvement. Maintain a student-first orientation while recognizing the needs and perspectives of the educators and communities Blue Engine serves. Core Responsibilities: Level 3: Drive impact for partners through effective implementation of Blue Engine’s products Competencies and Experience Required: Individuals demonstrate proficiency in the following competencies: Bachelor’s Degree required K–12 Experience: 5+ years of K–12 teaching experience with demonstrated impact on student outcomes, plus 2+ years of instructional coaching, school leadership, or related implementation leadership experience. Coaching experience in special education, multilingual education, and/or tiered intervention strongly preferred. Coaching & Developing Others: Demonstrated ability to deepen educators’ and leaders’ skills and shift behaviors and mindsets through technical and adaptive coaching. Experience building strong coaching relationships that lead to observable changes in practice; comfort coaching across multiple content areas and grade levels. Influencing & Motivating Others: Ability to navigate varied school and district contexts, build trusted relationships, and cultivate investment and engagement among stakeholders across roles and identities. Project Management: Demonstrated ability to organize and manage complex work across multiple partners and priorities, maintain a dynamic schedule, coordinate resources and stakeholders, and reliably meet commitments and deadlines. Unpacking Root Causes: Ability to analyze quantitative and qualitative evidence to identify root causes, strengths, and barriers; define problems; and develop actionable solutions responsive to local context. Setting & Managing Expectations: Communicates clear expectations, coordinates and delegates work effectively, and follows through to achieve shared goals. Functional Expertise: Strong knowledge of inclusive instruction and K–12 instructional systems, with expertise in special education, multilingual education, RTI/MTSS, and/or tiered academic intervention strongly preferred. Familiarity with nonprofit management and applying a strategic lens to problem-solving is a plus. Compensation This role sits in Job Level 3 within our compensation structure, with a starting salary range of $99,311 - $110, 345. Blue Engine provides comprehensive benefits. Compensation for this role will depend on experience, demonstrated performance on core competencies, and alignment with internal equity. Blue Engine offers a comprehensive benefits plan (through JustWorks, a PEO), including employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance, with most dependent costs subsidized. Other benefits include six weeks of paid time off, a 403(b) plan with employer matching, an FSA plan, commuter benefits, and a flexible work environment. To Apply Submit your application (resume & application questions) via the link below. We will review applications on a rolling basis.

review_candidates.description: Descripción de la empresa Globalem es una empresa con más de 10 años de experiencia en el sector energético, especializada en el desarrollo, diseño, construcción, almacenamiento, operación y mantenimiento de sistemas solares fotovoltaicos. Trabajamos con clientes que exigen altos estándares de calidad, reforzando nuestro compromiso con la independencia energética y los proyectos sostenibles. Contamos con un Sistema de Gestión Integral en Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo, Calidad y Medio Ambiente, orientado al cumplimiento de requisitos contractuales, la satisfacción de la clientela y la prevención de lesiones. Apostamos por la mejora continua, la prevención de la contaminación y el uso eficiente de los recursos, cumpliendo la normativa legal y optimizando procesos mediante indicadores de gestión. Además, promovemos una cultura preventiva, la participación activa de las personas trabajadoras y la reducción de la huella de carbono mediante tecnologías sostenibles, fortaleciendo la resiliencia de nuestros procesos frente al cambio climático. Descripción del puesto Como Director de construcción de parques fotovoltaicos, liderarás la planificación, ejecución y control de la construcción de proyectos solares fotovoltaicos, asegurando el cumplimiento de plazos, presupuesto, calidad y normativa aplicable. Coordinarás equipos de ingeniería, obra y subcontratas, supervisando el avance en campo, la correcta instalación de equipos y la gestión de recursos materiales y humanos. Tendrás que revisar y aprobar planes de obra, informes de avance, certificaciones y documentación técnica, garantizando la alineación con las especificaciones del proyecto y las políticas de seguridad y medio ambiente de la empresa. Participarás en la gestión de riesgos, la resolución de incidencias en obra y la interlocución con clientes, proveedores y autoridades locales. Este es un puesto a tiempo completo en modalidad híbrida, con base en Bogotá, D.C., combinando trabajo presencial en oficina y visitas a obra con cierta flexibilidad para trabajar desde casa. Requisitos Formación universitaria en ingeniería (preferiblemente eléctrica, industrial, civil, energética o afín) y experiencia sólida en dirección de proyectos de construcción, idealmente en parques fotovoltaicos o infraestructuras energéticas. Aptitudes en gestión de proyectos: planificación de obra, control de costes, gestión de contratos, seguimiento de cronogramas, manejo de herramientas de planificación (MS Project, Primavera u otras) y reporting a dirección. Aptitudes técnicas en energía solar fotovoltaica: conocimiento de diseño básico de SSFV, componentes principales (paneles, inversores, estructuras, sistemas de almacenamiento), normativa aplicable y estándares de calidad. Aptitudes en gestión de equipos y liderazgo: capacidad para coordinar equipos multidisciplinares, gestionar subcontratas, fomentar la colaboración
